claims.claim: Woodcock calls Le Guin's a style of crystalline clarity and functional flexibility.
claims.source: George Woodcock, quoted by John R. Pfeiffer in Joe De Bolt, ed., Ursula K. Le Guin: Voyager to Inner Lands and to Outer Space (Kennikat Press, 1979)
claims.quote: a style of crystalline clarity and functional flexibility

claims.claim: Pfeiffer calls the oral elements of the style of A Wizard of Earthsea a superb vehicle.
claims.source: John R. Pfeiffer, in Joe De Bolt, ed., Ursula K. Le Guin: Voyager to Inner Lands and to Outer Space (1979)
claims.quote: The oral elements of the style of WOE

claims.claim: Dirda says Le Guin gives her prose music occasionally through the use of alliteration and assonance.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, NEA Big Read teacher's guide to A Wizard of Earthsea (2008)
claims.quote: through the use of alliteration and assonance

claims.claim: A review of Tehanu reprinted in Children's Literature Review says Le Guin's style is as pellucid as ever.
claims.source: An unsigned review of Tehanu, reprinted in Children's Literature Review vol. 28 (Gale, 1992)
claims.quote: Le Guin's style is as pellucid as ever

claims.claim: Cogell's bibliography records a review calling Le Guin's style in one book different from her preceding works.
claims.source: Elizabeth Cummins Cogell, Ursula K. Le Guin: A Primary and Secondary Bibliography (G. K. Hall, 1983)
claims.quote: Le Guin's style is different from her preceding works

claims.claim: Juliette Wade observes that the archival header opening The Left Hand of Darkness contains no verbs at all.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: Notice that there are no verbs in this excerpt

claims.claim: Wade argues that the verbless archival header removes every actor and leaves what she calls a sourceless truth.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: leaving us with a sourceless truth

claims.claim: Wade identifies the register of the novel's archival header as that of the notes heading a scientific report.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: the notes that would head a scientific report

claims.claim: Wade reads the header's dating line as showing that the institution keeps its own measurement of time.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: it also dictates its own measurement of time
claims.page: paragraph on the number of alien names

claims.claim: Wade counts three distinct voices in the opening page of The Left Hand of Darkness, of which the archival header is the second.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: This is a voice of ultimate authority

claims.claim: The Left Hand of Darkness opens with a filing header that names an archive and a document number before any sentence with a verb.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: From the Archives of Hain. Transcript of Ansible Document

claims.claim: Genly Ai's first sentence names the document he is writing as a report before it narrates anything.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: I’ll make my report as if I told a story

claims.claim: The report's opening concedes that its account is neither wholly the reporter's nor told by him alone.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: The story is not all mine, nor told by me alone

claims.claim: The report fixes its starting point by an ordinal day of a numbered year before naming any person or place.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: It starts on the 44th diurnal of the Year 1491

claims.claim: A local timekeeping custom is stated as a bare present-tense sentence of seven ordinary words.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: It is always the Year One here
